checksums.name: global_header_checksum
checksums.formula_detail: u32 sum = 0; for i in [4,size): sum += buf[i]; stored little-endian at buf[0..3]. size=8 for this record.

checksums.formula_detail: Same sum8 primitive, size=0x14 (20 bytes) for this record.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Overwrite ranking_table entry 0's packed-name field (0x0020-0x0025) with a different 6-bit-packed ASCII string, then repair the checksum at 0x001c.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If a UI reads this table for display, the displayed name/initials at this table position should change, confirming the ranking-table semantic hypothesis.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Corrupt the ranking_table checksum at 0x001c without repairing it.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: On next boot, the table should be detected invalid and reset to all-zero (blank) entries via FUN_0803b250-equivalent logic.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Toggle each bit of the slot0 flag byte at 0x0ba4 individually, repairing the slot0 checksum (0x0ba0) after each change.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Bits forced by FUN_0803b634's masks (0,1,2,3,4,5,6,8) should revert on the next re-init pass; any surviving bit is a live gameplay setting.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write non-zero bytes at increasing offsets past 0x0d08 (0x0d20, 0x0d80, ...) with a correctly recomputed checksum at 0x0d00 for each candidate size.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Identifies the exact size boundary at which the game's reader (func_0x0803b8e4) stops accepting the record, resolving the open size question.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Write a recognizable 0xAA marker with a correct sum8 checksum at candidate base 0x1c08 for the 0x2400-byte record.
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: If the marker survives validation after reload, this confirms the base address of the large record; if rejected, rules out this candidate offset.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Truncate the .sav to only the primary 16KiB half (remove the 0x4000-0x7fff backup bank entirely).
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Exercises FUN_0803b040's backup-fallback path under a worst-case missing-backup condition; expected to force a full FUN_0803ba04 reset since every record's backup read will also fail.

open_questions: Exact base SRAM address and checksum boundary of the 0x2400-byte record written by FUN_0803b968.
Exact size of the record at absolute offset 0x0d00 written by FUN_0803b8a8 (bounded only as >=8 bytes from the checksum header).
Bit-level meaning of the flag byte/word at slot offset +4/+5 within each car-profile slot (only the forced-reset bits are known from static analysis).
Semantic role of the 16-byte config2 payload at 0x000c-0x001b (all-zero in the only available sample).
Why FUN_0803b968's RAM-side argument is used undereferenced while every sibling writer dereferences its RAM pointer; could indicate a static buffer rather than pointer-to-pointer, unconfirmed.
The specific in-ROM constant that FUN_0803b108 compares the global-header magic payload against (iRam0803b13c) was not resolved in this extraction window.

Six external stub functions (func_0x0803b208, func_0x0803b318, func_0x0803b4c0, func_0x0803b7d0, func_0x0803b8e4, func_0x0803b9a4, func_0x0803bdf8) that appear to be per-record checksum-verify readers analogous to FUN_0803b108 were not decompiled in this packet's extraction window.

Only one .sav sample (saves/cap-00-future-0.sav) was present in this workspace despite the packet's own metadata listing 6 captures; cross-save diffing to disambiguate gameplay-mutable fields from reset-constants was not possible this round.
